resolved_questions.Q1_split_ratio_when_caps_diverge: Always split at the smaller of the two products' current frequency caps (e.g. both 2 nights/week even once a ramped retinoid would otherwise qualify for 4). In practice this always evaluates to 2/week for the one real pairing today, since the exfoliant side's flat EXFOLIANT_TREATMENT_MAX_DAYS cap never exceeds 2.
resolved_questions.Q2_persistence_across_regenerations: Persist via the existing trackingStore override-list pattern (addOverride/overrides/currentOverrideHash), the same mechanism phase-07's 'Add anyway' already uses. A new dedicated store field was pre-approved but found unnecessary during design -- the rival is mechanically just 'a reserved product forced back in', so 'Alternate automatically' reuses addOverride verbatim on the rival's productId. Zero new persisted surface, a strictly lower-footprint outcome than what was approved -- see progress/day-split-alternation.md log for the disclosed simplification.
resolved_questions.Q3_pre_existing_manual_scheduledDays: Silently overwritten on 'Alternate automatically' tap. No new EngineInput/SkeletonInput visibility into the currently-saved Routine[] is added to detect or preserve a prior manual edit.
resolved_questions.Q4_multiple_same_cycleClass_rivals: Only the single best-ranked candidate of the losing cycleClass is ever detected/offered per period (today's existing tiebreak order). Every other same-class product keeps the plain cumulative_active_cap reserve treatment. Settled as a tech-design Assumption, not a recurring open question.

key_findings_from_planning: The 'caps differ' scenario is the steady state, not an edge case: bha has no adaptation ramp and aha/bha both always get the flat EXFOLIANT_TREATMENT_MAX_DAYS=2 cap when selected as treatment; retinoid (native serum format) has no such flat cap and purely follows its own adaptation.phases ramp (2/wk -> 4/wk -> uncapped after 8 applications). Asymmetric caps are the norm past a user's ~4-week initial retinoid ramp.
